To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the response of REITS to unexpected changes in macroeconomic variables varies across the three REIT categories; (2) the response of equity REIT returns to changes in macroeconomic state variables is consistent with the Chen, Roll, & Ross (1986) findings; and (3) REITs are not a good hedge for inflation.

(a) the responses of the REITs to the unexpected change in the broader market are not significantly different from zero, (b) the responses of equity REIT excess returns are significantly positive to unexpected changes in real growth and significantly negative to unexpected changes in default risk, and (c) the responses of mortgage REIT excess returns and hybrid REIT excess returns, in general, are significantly negative to the unexpected changes in the term structure of interest rate.
the REIT excess returns are sensitive to unexpected changes in macroeconomic state variables.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the response of RET excess returns to unexpected shocks to macroeconomic variables.
the response of RET excess returns to shocks to the broader stock market and macroeconomic state variables.
the identification of the response of REITS to unexpected changes in macroeconomic variables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
REITs are affected differently by the various shocks to macroeconomic variables depending on the classification of the REIT.
there is little evidence that macroeconomic state variables have a systematic impact on REITs.
REITs are not as sensitive to macroeconomic shocks as the stock market.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the response of REITS to macroeconomic shocks is not as uniform as previously believed.
the risk premium of the three broad classifications of REITs are influenced by the macroeconomic state variables in a different manner.

the responses of REIT excess return to shocks are not uniform across the different types of REITs and that the results of the generalized impulse response are sensitive to the lag length of the autoregressive model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single macroeconomic state variable that is consistently significant across all three broad REIT classification.
the risk premium of all three types of REITs is significantly influenced by macroeconomic state variables.
REITs respond differently to macroeconomic state variable shocks.
